summary: Operator-precedence bug in priority expression evaluator causes incorrect queueing of P1s
description: Summary: Starting 2026-03-09 we observed a rise in missed P1 SLAs where tickets with explicit P1 conditions in the priority expression were evaluated as lower priority and routed to the 'standard' queue. Impact: Several P1 and escalated issues reached first-response SLA breaches over the last 36 hours. Root cause hypothesis: the expression evaluator used by the rule-compiler appears to treat OR with higher precedence than AND in some compiled execution paths, causing expressions like '(env == "prod" OR customer_tier == "enterprise") AND sla_hours <= 2' to be evaluated incorrectly as 'env == "prod" OR (customer_tier == "enterprise" AND sla_hours <= 2)'. This changes the boolean logic and drops intended P1s out of fast paths.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a rule in staging with priority expression: (env == 'prod' OR customer_tier == 'enterprise') AND sla_hours <= 2
Send a synthetic ticket matching env=prod, customer_tier='self_serve', sla_hours=1
Observe which queue the rule-engine assigns (expected: p1-fasttrack / actual: standard)
Repeat in pairing session with a debug build of the evaluator and enable expression tracing

comments: Maya Chen (Support): Noticed 8 P1 tickets were routed to standard queue over last 12h, opened this ticket after comparing rule traces.
Arjun Patel (SRE): Reproduced locally using a minimal expression. Compiler bytecode ordering looked suspicious — OR op emitted before the AND group was bound.
Elena Rivera (Platform Eng): I pushed a temporary guard that forces parentheses-respectful evaluation in the interpreter — staging tests green so far. Will open PR for compiler fix.
Maya Chen (Support): Please track any customers impacted separately; I alerted CS leads and started manual re-route for open impacted tickets.
investigation_notes: Confirmed reproduction in both Python-based interpreter and optimized AOT-compiled path. AOT path used a different precedence table (bug introduced in commit 7f2c8b1).
Unit test missing for mixed AND/OR expressions without explicit parentheses — adding coverage.
Hypothesis: parser emitted correct AST but codegen flattened binary ops and used left-to-right reduction without respecting canonical boolean precedence.
Experiment: forcing explicit parentheses in codegen fixed all failing cases in staging (see branch feature/expr-precedence-guard).
resolution: Workaround applied: added runtime parentheses guard in router interpreter (rolled to prod us-east at 2026-03-12T04:30Z) which restores correct evaluation order for affected rules. Long-term fix: merged PR #3124 that updates the compiler precedence table and adds unit tests + fuzz tests for expression combinations. Rollout plan: gradual deploy of compiler fix to canary, then prod after 24h of monitoring. Post-deploy verification checklist included in linked Confluence page.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Guard deployed to prod/us-east — immediate reduction in misrouted P1s observed (0 incidents in 8h window).
2026-03-13: Compiler fix merged to main (PR 3124). Canary build in eu-west for additional validation.
Follow-up: add a telemetry alert for boolean-eval mismatches (new metric: expr_evaluation_discrepancy_count) and schedule a postmortem in #support blameless-rotation.
Owner for follow-ups: Arjun Patel (engineering) and Maya Chen (support ops)
